page: Amazon Web Services r9g.medium is a memory-optimized instance tier within the ninth-generation Graviton family. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and utilizes a custom 64-bit Arm processor clocked at 3.3 GHz. The instance configuration provides 1 dedicated physical core mapping directly to 1 vCPU with 1 thread per core, ensuring consistent execution without multithreading contention.

System memory measures 8.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU allocation ratio characteristic of memory-oriented profiles. The server does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating remote network-attached volumes for data retention. Network performance is defined with a baseline bandwidth capacity of 1 Gbps, and there are no complementary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware GPUs included.

Relative to standard general-purpose profiles, the r9g.medium provides higher memory density per compute core, maximizing cost efficiency for applications bound by memory footprint rather than parallel processing power. Tradeoffs include limited compute scaling due to the single-core constraint and reliance on remote storage for all input-output operations. This profile fits small in-memory key-value stores, lightweight database testing environments, cache nodes, and single-threaded data preparation jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.medium is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a single dedicated AWS Graviton physical core running at 3.3 GHz on the arm64 architecture, supporting one virtual CPU without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB, producing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive workloads that require modest compute resources. The instance contains no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistence requirements, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. With zero GPU acceleration, the hardware footprint is tailored for lightweight workloads that benefit from higher memory density than standard general-purpose offerings. The architecture offers cost efficiency by pairing an energy-efficient Arm processor with generous memory capacity per thread. Workload suitability includes entry-level in-memory data caches, small transactional databases, background processing workers, and lightweight microservices requiring memory buffers.
